title: Roll a heavy block on loose rollers
instruction: In the top camera view, roll the blue block to the right until all of it lies between the two green strips and within their length, at rest on at least two of the three orange rollers. The rollers are loose: carry a roller from behind the block to the front of it whenever the block needs one. The block must never touch the table. At the end, let go and move both arms at least 5 cm away from the block and the rollers.
context: Riggers and warehouse workers move loads too heavy to lift by rolling them over round bars, carrying each freed bar from the back to the front.
setup: World frame: x forward from the arms, y to the robot's left, z up; positions are object centres. Table: fixed flat tabletop, oak-coloured wood, 110 x 130 x 6 cm, top at z 0.7475 m. Block: rigid rectangular solid, blue-painted wood shell with internal steel ballast, 12 x 16 x 8 cm (x, y, z), 3 kg in total (solid wood of this size would be about 1 kg, so the ballast is needed), centred at x 0.25, y 0.07, its underside 3.0 cm above the table, resting on the rollers. Rollers: three loose identical orange-painted softwood dowels, 3 cm diameter, 26 cm long with rounded ends, 80 g each, lying along x, centred at x 0.25, y 0.005, 0.07 and 0.135 m, on the table. Strips: two fixed flat green vinyl tape strips stuck to the table, 2 x 22 cm, 1 mm thick, centred at x 0.105 and 0.395 m, y -0.14 m. Arms: two YAM 6-joint arms with parallel-jaw grippers (94 mm maximum opening), metal and plastic links, rubber-like finger pads, bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m, z 0.75 m, starting in the ready pose with the grippers open. Camera stand: fixed mock stand behind the arms, painted metal, foot 11 x 11 x 1.6 cm centred at x -0.236, y -0.009 m at table-top height, overhanging the table's back edge (the table spans x -0.19 to 0.91 m, y -0.65 to 0.65 m), 2.4 cm diameter mast; the top camera and two wrist cameras are as the adapter's station defines them. Nothing else is on the table. In the simulator all contacts use the adapter's material, friction 1.2 static and 1.0 dynamic, and wood, paint, tape and rubber are not modelled separately.
scoring: 1.0, and the trial ends on that step: on 21 consecutive control steps, which is 1 s from the first to the last at 20 Hz, all of these held together, with no failure below having happened. The block's world-axis bounding box lies between the inner edges of the two strips and within their length (x 0.115 to 0.385 m, y -0.25 to -0.03 m). It is tilted at most 5 degrees. Its centre speed plus its spin times its 3D half-diagonal (10.8 cm), using the simulator's velocities, is under 1 cm/s. At least 2 rollers are under it. Every measured arm point is at least 5 cm from the block and from every roller. Any step that fails one of these restarts the count. At a control rate other than 20 Hz the number of steps changes so that the count still spans 1 s. A roller is under the block when its centre lies inside the block's bounding box in x and y, and is at most 5 mm above where it lies on the table, 5 mm included; contact forces are not read. The measured arm points are the collision-mesh vertices of every link except the fixed base, placed by the simulator's link poses; points on a mesh face between vertices are not measured, and an arm link missing from the simulator's poses counts as not clear. Each is measured against the world-axis bounding boxes of the block and rollers; each box is the object's local box (a roller's is 26 x 3 x 3 cm) with its corners moved by the object's pose, so a rolled roller's box is up to about 6 mm larger than the roller. This shows the arms are away from the block and rollers. It does not read contact forces or the gripper opening, so a gripper closed on nothing and held away counts as let go. A trial that does not end this way gets the score of its last step: 0.5 if the block's centre is now at least 15 cm along -y from where it was at the first evaluated step, 0.25 at 6 cm, else 0; this is the current position, not the furthest reached. Score 0 on any control step the block tilts over 5 degrees. Score 0 for the rest of the trial, even if the layout is put back, once any of these has happened: its underside (the lowest corner of its bounding box) is under 2 cm or over 3.5 cm above the table; it tilts over 10 degrees; its centre moves faster than 20 cm/s by the simulator's velocity; or its slip total exceeds 2 cm. Slip: a block rolling on rollers moves twice as far as they do. On each step, take the block's move along y and the mean move along y of the rollers now under it. The slip of that step is the difference between the block's move and twice the rollers' mean move, taken as a size, and no more than the size of the block's move; with no roller under the block it is the whole of the block's move. The total adds these up over the trial and allows no more than 2 cm: a slip total of more than 2 cm means the block was carried, slid or dragged, not rolled. Moving rollers around under a still block adds nothing. With a tape measure this is the rule that rollers under the block move half as far as the block does. Only a new trial clears a failure, seen as the environment's step count falling back to below its previous value. The adapter's settling steps before the first control step are not evaluated: evaluation starts at the environment's step 11 at 20 Hz, and nothing the policy does can happen before it. Everything is evaluated at the control steps, 20 Hz; what happens between them is not seen.
reset_notes: Put the block and rollers back at the listed positions with both arms in their ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX on CPU; capsules stand in for the rollers. Linear damping on the block and linear and angular damping on the rollers approximate rolling resistance, so the block may coast less than on real rollers. Contacts use the adapter's default high-friction material, not measured wood. One fixed layout. Arm clearance and the step count are read through a wrapper this task file puts on the adapter's private scene module at import.
